text: This is Migration-in-a-box. It turns PDFs, Excel and CSV files into one clean Excel sheet for your new system. Everything runs inside your browser, so your files are never uploaded.
First, drag your files in. Here are six G S T invoices, an Excel stock list and a scanned invoice. Each one is read in a second or two, and you can see how many rows it found.
The scanned invoice is only a picture, so I press Read scanned pages. The app reads it with OCR, right on this computer, and marks it so you remember to check the numbers.
Now the template, which decides the columns of your Excel. I switch on Auto, and it suggests the best free template for these files. One click on Use it.

And the preview is ready. Every item gets one complete line: invoice number, date, both G S T I Ns, the description, and the item type, worked out from the description. Scrolling right, there is the quantity, rate, amount, and the taxable value, C G S T, S G S T and grand total. The proof line confirms every invoice adds up.

You can also build your own layout. I remove all columns, then click the fields I want: invoice number, invoice date, description, quantity and amount. Setting a column to Date writes every date the same way, day first.
Or describe the Excel you want to the AI helper. Before anything is sent, this box shows exactly what would leave your computer: only the column names, never your files.
Finally, save the template in your Library to reuse it next time, choose one sheet per file if you like, and download the Excel, with a proof sheet included. That is Migration-in-a-box.
